feature: A component sheet on one grid, with looks that mean their state
summary: Every look in a component sheet now starts at its column's left edge, a state keeps its column from one section to the next, and wide components take whole columns instead of a grid of their own. Ask also stops drawing an Off checkbox with its tick, an Off switch in blue or near black, a Disabled field darker than its Default, empty cards, and more than four type sizes.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a blank 1440 x 1024 picture and press Ask.

try.do: Press Ask and type: create a table of apple like quality base components that show different states and text
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Run your eye down the Default column: every look and header starts on the same left edge.
Find the Off toggle and Off checkbox: the toggle is grey and the box is empty.
Ask for: Make a component sheet for a website's design system: buttons, text fields, cards and navigation, each labelled, with a title.
Ask the Photonz skill in an agent session for the same two sheets and compare.
Look at the skill's design sheet: wide navigation bars and cards start on the button columns above them.
Press Command Z once: the whole sheet goes.

evaluate: Do looks starting at their column's left edge read better than looks centred in their cells did?
When a section has fewer states (Off and On under four button columns), does it read as part of one grid?
Is a card that takes every other column, under five button columns, lined up enough?
Do the Off and Disabled looks now read as off and disabled at a glance?
rough: Not at the bar yet, so the task stays open. Skill (rubric f5ae1562): the user's request 86, judge 8, 8, 7, 8, 8 (was 88.8 with 8 on every line in one earlier run, 77.6 to 86.4 in others); the design sheet 81.2 and 85.6, judge 8, 8, 7, 8, 9 and 8, 7, 8, 8, 9 (was 85.2, aligned 7). Ask on this Mac: the user's request 58.3, judge 6, 7, 7, 5, 6 (was 48 and 57.3); the design sheet 77.2 and 79.2, judge 6 to 8 (was 37.7 and 49.4). Before: 2026-10-20-user-ask-component-sheet-mess.png.

What holds Ask back is still its own drawings: a segmented control with one option and looks named Selected 1, 2, 3, two rows both called Button, a slider whose states look the same, a tab icon that is a blob, and once more a blue Off toggle that the new Off check did not catch (the same call rebuilt by hand is caught, so the model sent something the trace does not show).
Judges still mark aligned 7 when one section has more columns than another (four buttons over five fields): the grid is shared, but a short row ends early.
The name chips the canvas puts over each component copy cover the header row in the window picture. Already its own task: the-name-chips-over-component-copies-stay-clear.
